summary: RetailerX morning fanout deadlock causing retry amplification and duplicate completions — post-incident follow-up
description:
Issue summary: During morning traffic ramp (approx 08:45-09:20 PDT) RetailerX observed a sharp increase in 5xx and duplicate completions for chat and batch completion requests. Customer reported application-level retries and duplicate downstream events causing order duplication alerts and billing anomalies.

Impact: Approximately 18% of RetailerX production requests (targeting rw-instruct-13b-quantized) experienced long tail latencies >10s or 5xx errors. Several streaming sessions were cut and reconnected, producing duplicated completions reported by the customer. RetailerX escalated to enterprise support due to real customer orders being affected.

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-03-10 08:42 PDT: RetailerX first alerts via support channel and sent sample request ids.
- 2026-03-10 08:44 PDT: Automated alert from latency SLOs (api-gateway) fires; paging SRE.
- 2026-03-10 08:47 PDT: Initial mitigation applied: enforce per-customer circuit breaker at router to limit concurrent inflight requests.
- 2026-03-10 08:55 PDT: Observed reduced 5xx rate but duplicate completions continued for a subset of requests.
- 2026-03-10 09:10 PDT: Root cause hypothesis formed; temporary scheduler tweak deployed to break request fanout.
- 2026-03-10 09:20 PDT: Traffic normalized and customer confirmed reduction in duplicates.
- 2026-03-11: Post-incident follow-up investigation and permanent patch rollout completed.

Steps to reproduce (investigation reproducer):
1) Send high-concurrency batched calls that trigger cross-shard fanout to rw-instruct-13b-quantized with prefix cache enabled.
2) Inject a short scheduler stall condition (simulated CPU spike on scheduler worker) and observe request queue growth.
3) If router-side retry/backoff windows are misaligned with scheduler drain, queued requests are retried and can be delivered twice when the stall clears.

Logs & evidence provided: request ids (sample): rdx-20260310-8a7e, rdx-20260310-8a9f, rdx-20260310-90b4. Grafana charts: latency_p99 by customer, router_retry_rate, scheduler_queue_depth. Link to live playbacks and HAR artifacts included in Confluence postmortem.

Customer impact summary for RetailerX: duplicate downstream events (order webhook fired twice), elevated token consumption (billing exposure ~+12% for the window), and short-lived UI errors. RetailerX requested a credit assessment for the affected window; finance/CSR looped in.

Mitigation taken during incident: temporary per-customer inflight limit at router, reduced default router retry attempts from 3 -> 1 for affected customer, and an emergency scheduler configuration toggle to prefer draining oldest requests first. These reduced amplification within 15 minutes and restored normal behavior after further tuning.

Permanent fixes implemented: scheduler patch to avoid request coalescing deadlocks under high queue pressure; router/backoff alignment so retries use exponential jitter tied to scheduler drain state; added failing-metric alarms for duplicate completion rate and per-customer inflight token accounting.

Follow-up ask from customer: formal post-incident write-up, confirmation of billing credit, and recommended best practices for their integration (per-tenant concurrency limits, client-side idempotency keys).
comments: Support (Marisol): Received initial flagged request ids and screenshots of duplicate webhooks. Engaged SRE escalation at 08:44 PDT.

SRE (Liam): Confirmed router retry spike and scheduler queue growth; applied temporary inflight limit and lowered retries for RetailerX. Noted that draining order resolved duplicates for most sessions.
RetailerX (Ben Collins): Thanks — we still saw two order events for two customers after the change at ~09:00 PDT. Can you confirm if those will be credits?
SRE (Liam): Investigating root cause; adding postmortem and draft credit amount for finance. ETA for permanent fix: 48 hours. Will follow up with runbook improvements.
CS (Priya Singh): Escalated billing request to finance with preliminary exposure estimate +12% tokens during 08:30-09:30 PDT. Finance assigned to ticket FIN-2384.
Customer (Ben): RetailerX confirms that after the rollback at 09:20 PDT duplicates stopped. Awaiting postmortem and credit confirmation.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: autoscaler-induced scheduler jitter causing request starvation on a small subset of scheduler workers.
Observed scheduler_queue_depth spike correlated with a new scheduler release (rollout completed 2026-03-09 02:00 UTC) that changed coalescing semantics for batched requests.

Router retry policy did not observe scheduler backpressure signals; retries were retried aggressively and then reconciled when the scheduler cleared, producing duplicate completions in client-visible streams.
Reproducer created in staging by simulating scheduler stall and high fanout; confirmed duplicate completions when router retries were aggressive and prefix cache rehydration occurred.
No evidence of data corruption or model state issues; duplicates are delivery-level only.
resolution: Rolled back coalescing change in scheduler (patch ID: platform@release-2026.03.11:7f2a1bd).
Deployed router change to respect scheduler drain signals for retry/backoff alignment and added exponential jitter tied to drain state.
Added per-customer inflight caps (configurable) and defaulted RetailerX to a conservative cap for 72 hours post-incident.
Created new alerting: duplicate_completion_rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m and per-customer token surge detection.
Finance and CS agreed on a provisional credit: 12% of tokens billed for 2026-03-10 08:30-09:30 PDT pending final audit (ticket FIN-2384).
Postmortem published and shared with RetailerX: https://confluence.redwood.ai/postmortems/SUP-824568-retailerx.
postincident_action_items: ENG-3456: Implement deterministic scheduler backpressure signal in router (owner: Liam Chen, due: 2026-03-19)
SRE-118: Expand per-customer observability dashboards to include inflight_count and duplicate_completion_rate (owner: Aisha Khan, due: 2026-03-16)
CS-77: Confirm final billing credit and close FIN-2384 with customer finance (owner: Priya Singh, due: 2026-03-15)
DOC-22: Update Playbook: guidance for customers on idempotency keys and recommended per-tenant concurrency settings (owner: DevRel Team, due: 2026-03-25)
OPS-9: Add canary gating for any future scheduler coalescing changes (owner: Platform Release Lead, due: 2026-04-01)
